text: One of your program’s components will be outsourced. You are currently preparing a Statement Of Work (SOW) in order to send RFPs to the qualified sellers list. One of your steering committee members approaches you and asks you to grant the contract to a seller that he knows will do a great job. You find out that the seller has been removed from the qualified sellers list and you inform the steering committee member, however, he insists on selecting him. What should you do in this case?
choices: A. Escalate to steering committee
B. Escalate to executive management
C. Escalate to sponsor
D. Inform sponsor, add the seller to the qualified sellers list and continue your process

text: You have been managing a program with a low risk tolerance and you have been managing potential risks closely in order to ensure proper mitigation. A new CEO joined your company and he is well known to take more risks than his precedent CEO. What should be you first course of action?
choices: A. Revise and update the business case
B. Revise and update the charter
C. Revise and update the roadmap
D. Continue as planned

text: Program manager is the champion for change. The program manager integrates the change in the most efficient way in order to ensure proper realization and sustainment of benefits. During the course of the program and due to uncertainty, a new change needs to be integrated in the program. You then
choices: A. Analyze and update the benefits realization and sustainment plans
B. Analyze roadmap
C. Escalate to steering committee
D. Continue as planned as changes are normal in a program

text: You are managing a sporting event in a rural village. After the event, you plan on leaving the sporting arena and gaming material for the village. Few important stakeholders in the village are still against it. What is your best course of action?
choices: A. Accept the fact that some of the stakeholders will be negative and you need to ignore them
B. Add the negative stakeholders to program steering committee

C. Meet with them one on one if you can or as a group, listen to them and let them know that they will have a sporting arena after the event and that multiple jobs will be offered to the youth during the event.
D. Focus only on positive stakeholders

text: You are in the definition phase of your program to deliver 5 new ice cream flavors and you are aware that this phase is the most important phase in order to guide the remainder of the program. You have finished the stakeholders’ analysis and have prepared the stakeholder engagement strategy and plan. What is next?
choices: A. Stakeholder engagement
B. Update stakeholder register
C. Issue the stakeholder engagement plan
D. Update business case

text: You have been managing your program successfully and you have been doing a good job integrating the individual components to maximize the delivery of benefits. You have been integrating costs, schedules and effort of components throughout the program. As a program manager you develop and support the program integration management plan in order to
choices: A. Ensure operational alignment with program strategic objectives
B. Ensure continuation to the next phase
C. Prepare your master schedule
D. Preparing your program roadmap

text: During the planning phase, the program manager uses the scope baseline and the scope management plan to prepare the schedule management plan and derives, using the PWBS, the master schedule and management control points. Which of the below is part of the content of master schedule?
choices: A. Stakeholder engagement activities
B. Program-level risk mitigation activities
C. Individual component schedules
D. All of the options

text: You are mid-way through your program and you are now collecting performance information in preparation of the next checkpoint. A project manager approached you with an issue with one of his resources; the resource is always late and reluctant for any advice. What would you suggest to the project manager?
choices: A. Escalate to functional manager
B. Escalate to project CCB
C. Escalate to project steering committee
D. Escalate to program steering committee

text: You have been working hard to keep the program to launch the new remote car design to the market on track and you have been integrating multiple changes along the way in order to keep the program aligned with the organization's objectives and goals. Your program is to deliver soon. You sponsor approached you in order to implement a mandatory change. What should you do?
choices: A. Analyze the impact of the change and recommend a change request
B. Refuse to add changes as the program is nearing closure
C. Escalate to steering committee about the situation
D. Ask the component managers to send their feedback about implementing the change

text: You have been working hard to keep the program to launch the new remote car design to the market on track and you have been integrating multiple changes along the way in order to keep the program aligned with the organization's objectives and goals. Your program is to deliver soon. You sponsor approached you and asked you to add a change which he thinks is beneficial. You do not agree with the sponsor and know that the change will only result in wasting time. What should you do?
choices: A. Analyze the impact of the change and recommend a change request
B. Refuse to add changes as the program is nearing closure

text: You have been working hard to keep the program to launch the new remote car design to the market on track and you have been integrating multiple changes along the way in order to keep the program aligned with the organization's objectives and goals. choices: A. Analyze the impact of the change and recommend a change request
B. Refuse to add changes as the program is nearing closure
C. Escalate to steering committee about the situation and seek advice
D. Ask the component managers to send their feedback about implementing the change

text: You program to deliver the cancer drug to cure all the patients around the world has been performing as expected and you are nearing the closure phase. In your program, one component is already in the closure phase and has been completed under budget. What should you do?

B. Take the team out for lunch and build team morale

D. Return to sponsor

text: You are during the sixth month of your 2-years program and multiple changes are being reviewed in order to take go/no-go decisions on multiple components. One of the components has delivered the intended benefits and is already in the closure phase. Another component will need to undergo a big change in order to realign it with the program objectives. What is the first step that you will do next?
choices: A. Analyze change
B. Escalate to steering committee
C. Record change
D. Assign a team member to handle it

text: Programs normally use the procurement policies and procedures of the organization, unless the program has particular procurement specifications; in this case, the program manager will use the organization procurement processes and tailor them with the support from PMO to the program’s needs. B. RFI, RFP, RFQ, BC

text: You are the program manager of a complex program in a risk adverse company; during the last phase gate review, you realized that the program will not be able to deliver in the given benefits window and will probably be over budget when delivering the benefits. What is your best course of action?

B. Do a fast tracking
C. Do critical chain method
D. Continue as planned and try to fix the performance until the next phase gate review

text: When the program manager is assigned, normally the work on the program begins. In order to develop, validate, and assess the program objectives, priority, feasibility, readiness, and alignment to the organization’s strategic plan, you
choices: A. Evaluate the organization’s capability by consulting with organizational leaders
B. Design business case
C. Meet with stakeholders
D. Define scope statement

text: You are appointed as a program manager for the development of new remote cars. The cars need to be available for a two-hour play time on a full battery and has to be pushed to the market within one year in order to beat competition. choices: A. Continue as planned with components transitions and closures
B. Re-baseline budget
C. Conduct a phase gate review

text: Different stakeholders have different interests, expectations and needs. Some data is confidential for a certain group of stakeholders while being authorized for others. Which document do you present to him?
choices: A. Program charter
B. Scope statement
C. Business case
D. Benefits management plan

text: Your program is mid-way through the delivery phase and it is performing as planned. So far, you have been managing the program successfully. choices: A. Impact vs. probability
B. Monte Carlo analysis
C. Qualitative techniques

text: You program is a low-priority program and right from the start of the program you noticed delays in supplying the program resources from the functional departments. What should you do in this case?
choices: A. Resource leveling
B. Escalate to sponsor
C. Escalate to steering committee

text: You are the program manager of a complex program in a risk adverse company; during the last phase gate review, you realized that the program will not be able to deliver in the given benefits window and will probably be over budget when delivering the benefits. choices: A. Update business case and close the program

text: Your stakeholders on your program to deliver the next-generation remote control car are interested in knowing the progress of a program in delivering its benefits. Using which of the below, the program manager tracks the benefits delivery progress and reports to stakeholders?
choices: A. Benefits management plan
B. Benefits register
C. Business case
D. Benefits list

text: Your company was outsourced by a client in order to manage a program to do a company restructuring. You were appointed as the program manager. You realize that many employees will lose their jobs following the restructuring. You should start by?
choices: A. Foster relationships with stakeholders

C. Understanding the organization culture

text: You are in program definition phase and are currently evaluating program objectives relative to regulatory and legal constraints, social impacts, sustainability, cultural considerations, political, climate and ethical concerns. You do this in order to?
choices: A. Identify organizational benefits
B. Ensure stakeholder alignment and program deliverability
C. Obtain organizational leadership approval
D. Perform an initial risk assessment

text: The program manager tries throughout the program to resolve conflicts arising between stakeholders in order to maintain efficient benefits delivery. You notice that two of your sponsors are in conflict about buying or leasing a facility to be used by multiple components. What should be your best course of action?

choices: A. Considered a bribe and it should not be done

choices: A. The number of resources used in each program
